errors.text: The predicted segregation architecture is reversed: the target mechanism places low-surface-energy Au and Cu at the particle surface, whereas the hypothesis predicts Au/Cu-rich cores and Co/Ni/Pt-rich surfaces.

The hypothesis assigns disappearance of small particles primarily to Ostwald ripening and redeposition, predicting over 50% growth in average particle size; the target instead reports Au/Cu surface-shell melting and evaporation, producing an approximately 22% reduction in particle size.
The predicted bimodal, coarsened distribution and extensive phase-separated domains do not reproduce the observed widening associated with preferential loss and shrinkage of the smallest particles.

The cited evidence is generic to HEA synthesis or catalyst sintering and does not directly support the claimed critical size, 600 K threshold, elemental segregation direction, or Ostwald-ripening mechanism in AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles.
